text:
praveen: kicking off canary for release v2.7.3 to eu-west (10% -> 30% over 20m). keeping an eye on SLOs, please ack.

deploy-bot: Canary started: cb-7784. Target routes: /v1/generate (canary), /v1/embed (shadow). Traffic: 10% -> 30% in 3 steps. Logs and traces will be tagged: release:v2.7.3, canary:true.

maria: ack. i'll watch the p95/p99 dashboards and api-5xx. ping me if the error rate >0.6% sustained for 5m.

alex: noted — observability retention window set to 30m for this run (so we catch transient spikes). i'll keep an eye on per-route sampling.

metrics-bot: alert rule check: will fire if rolling 5m 5xx rate >0.6% AND traffic >= 5k rps. Current baseline: 0.12% 5m for eu-west /v1/generate.

praveen: first step rolled to 10% now. confirm dashboards loading for everyone? i see a tiny bump in the aggregate 5xx panel but nothing alarming.

dana: seeing spike on the embed service SLO dashboard — 2.1% at 1m. but logs show only 8 errors in last 5m. something's off, could be sampling/aggregation mismatch.

maria: +1. panels are based on sampled metrics and span sampling for embeds was recently lowered for cost savings. maybe the canary traffic is being under-sampled, inflating per-sample error ratio.

alex: good catch. checking trace sampling config: `observability.config.spans_sample_rate` for release:v2.7.3 was set to 0.01 for eu-west (1%). that explains the discrepancy — low sample size -> noisy error percentage.

praveen: ugh. did that change rollout to canaries only or global? it should not affect metrics used by SLOs.

alex: it was toggled as a feature flag during the last infra cost optimization. rollout targeted non-prod by mistake, but canary inherited the flag. flag key: `telemetry:low_span_sample_canary`.

deploy-bot: Canary step advanced to 20% (timestamp cb-7784-2). No automated rollback conditions triggered yet.

maria: recommended temporary mitigation: set spans_sample_rate=1.0 for release:v2.7.3 on eu-west for the canary tag. that will ensure accurate SLO math. will push change to feature flag now.

praveen: do it. also flip on route-level full sampling for `/v1/embed` specifically if possible.

alex: changing: `ffctl override telemetry:low_span_sample_canary --env=eu-west --release=v2.7.3 --value=1.0`

metrics-bot: flag change detected. new sampling rate: 100% for release:v2.7.3 (eu-west). Applying to live telemetry.

dana: after forcing full sampling, dashboard error rate for embed dropped to 0.18% 5m and traces show 6 errors across 5k requests — matches logs now. previous 2.1% was sampling noise.

oncall-sre: great triage. decision: continue canary to 30% but disable the low-sample cost flag for future canaries until we have a clearer telemetry plan. praveen, can you add a short note to the release and pin the canary variant in the release notes?

praveen: adding to release notes: "Investigated false-positive 5xx spike during canary due to low span sampling flag. Sampling restored to 100% for canary; monitoring panels verified. Recommending telemetry flag rollback for canary routes until rollout validation updated." Also pinning v2.7.3-canary for 2h.

maria: i'll close the transient alert ticket and annotate the SLO dashboard with the investigation link.

alex: follow-up action item: create a guard in the deploy pipeline that prevents telemetry-critical sampling flags from being enabled for canary releases (ticket: INFRA-1421).

praveen: ok continuing to 30% now. no further anomalies so far. will report final status when steady for 30m.

deploy-bot: Canary completed: cb-7784 done. Traffic at 30%. No automated rollback executed.

dana: thanks everyone. small postmortem note: cost savings flag interfered with observability. we can still enable sampling reduction for steady-state, but must exclude canaries in the rollout policy.

maria: resolved for now. will follow up with infra on INFRA-1421 and update runbook steps in changewindows/monitoring.md :thumbsup:

praveen: closing thread — rollforward approved. tagging release as rolled to 30% and scheduling full rollout next maintenance window unless any new alerts pop up.
